survey: The card shows a round glass plate of fruit on a wooden table, seen from in front and above at about 40°. The plate's rim is a smooth ellipse whose long axis runs across the picture, so the plate lies flat on the table. Its rim, its soft shadow toward the lower left and the diagonal table planks all agree with one raised camera. Watermelon wedge: stands on its rind at the back, with the red cut face turned toward the viewer and slightly up; the view is from above, so this face should look a little squashed, and it does, only slightly, which suits the stylised look. Orange half (back right): leans against the watermelon; its cut face is a rounded ellipse turned up and to the left, and the segment lines spread evenly from the centre. Orange wedge (front left): lies with its cut face up and toward the camera; the segment lines fan out from the core and the peel arc curves around the near side. Grapes: sit in a cluster in the middle and read as round balls (one measures 0.91 wide-to-tall), as expected. Strawberries and blueberries: rest along the front of the plate; their green leaf tops and the blueberries' crowns are seen from above, which matches the plate. Seeds and water droplets: the seeds are teardrop shapes, so their mixed tilts are normal, and the droplets follow the curve of the watermelon's surface. Everything is seen from the same raised angle, the cut faces shrink about as much as their surfaces turn away, and each piece of fruit rests on the plate at the plate's own angle.
